pairs_touching.notes_for_p3b: The shared surface word 'authority' overloads two senses corpus-wide (epistemic source-authority vs governance decision-authority); this pair is the clearest test case P1 itself flagged as unconfirmed. Worth checking other 'authority'-named labels in the corpus for the same overload if P3b aggregates across pairs.
pairs_touching.what_says_this: group_evidence (G0189, POSSIBLY-RELATION) is the corpus/extraction process's own stated uncertainty: rows using the label 'decision-authority' were repeatedly flagged unknown_candidate against 'authority-trust-source-reliability-knowledge-commitment', suspecting they might be the same object, 'not yet confirmed'. Inspecting actual content resolves this: A's full content (Authority(S,A,Ctx), Trust(source,context,task,time), Rel(S,A,Ctx,t), Commit_rho(...), s1 succeq_C s2) is entirely about epistemic source-reliability/evidence-weighting (Step 19) — a real-valued/ordered trust function over sources+context. B's sample content (S0001 ownership-gap finding; S0204 launch-instrument approval; S0234 'the PO/ARB is the reserved decision authority', four-stage chain Architecture proposal->Principal Architect recommendation->PO/ARB decision->Governance registration; S0288 F1 discipline separating capability from authorization; S0450 causal-vs-normative Wisdom Lens #7, AI must not silently collapse Evidence->Decision) is entirely about organizational/governance decision-rights (who may decide/approve). Zero dual-labeled rows across either full row set; no lineage_claims either direction. Different responsibility (epistemic source-trust modeling vs governance decision-rights) and no continuity shown between them despite the shared word 'authority' and the corpus's own flagged possible identity.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: A row defining ARB/PO decisions as a special case or instantiation of the Authority(S,A,Ctx) source-trust function (e.g. treating an ARB ruling as just another 'source' scored by the same trust model) would refute HOMONYM in favor of SPECIALIZATION; conversely a row where 'decision-authority' unknown_candidate rows are confirmed (not merely suspected) to belong to the authority-trust family would push toward SAME.

pairs_touching.what_says_this: The only group_evidence is an UNKNOWN-OBJECT-CANDIDATE row (S0202) naming BOTH decision-authority and decision-model as alternative possible matches for an unrelated third external finding ('decision-history-as-asset' from AKM/ADR literature), explicitly stating 'not clearly the same object as the corpus's own Engineering Decision Model or Decision Authority/ARB.' This establishes uncertainty about a third external object's match to either label -- it says nothing about whether decision-authority and decision-model relate to EACH OTHER.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: If a row directly compared decision-authority and decision-model's own definitions and found identity, refinement, or contradiction between them.

pairs_touching.notes_for_p3b: Both concepts use the word 'decision' but in different senses (authority-to-decide vs. category-of-act); insufficient positive evidence of either shared identity or deliberate separation to call HOMONYM outright -- defaulting to UNWITNESSED per protocol calibration guidance for weak-signal pairs.
pairs_touching.what_says_this: No shared source_ids, no dual-labeled rows, and no lineage_claims connect a and b anywhere in their full row sets (20 for a, 3 for b, neither truncated). Content-wise the two concepts operate in different registers: a (decision-authority) is a governance/organizational concept about WHO holds the right to decide (PO/ARB decision chains, session-completion authorization protocols, F1 capability-vs-authorization discipline); b (INV-002) is a constitutional epistemic invariant about a categorical distinction -- that the act of observing something is never itself the act of deciding on it (part of the TRANSFORMATION family alongside INV-001/003/004, registered at UM-24). The group's own why_grouped note is itself uncertain and possibly refers to a duplicate-registration concern for b's own INV-002 object under a different earlier batch, not necessarily a claim about a.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: If a specific row were found stating that the governance decision-authority chain (a) is itself an application/instance of the Observation!=Decision invariant (b) -- e.g. 'the ARB's decision right presupposes the Observation!=Decision boundary' -- that would establish a genuine dependency and move this out of UNWITNESSED.

pairs_touching.notes_for_p3b: The hedge in the P2a note itself ('may overlap ... or may not') should be preserved for P3b; this is a case where P1/P2a flagged genuine unresolved uncertainty rather than a specific claim.
pairs_touching.what_says_this: G0053 POSSIBLY-RELATION note is itself hedged: 'may overlap an already-registered general object of the same name from an earlier batch'. pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: A row directly stating decision-authority's ARB process instantiates or is governed by INV-003 as its defining invariant would raise this past UNWITNESSED.

pairs_touching.notes_for_p3b: Both share several identical source rows (S0288, S0304-S0322) reflecting the same broader governance saga; still no direct object-lineage claim.

rationale_evidence.statement: Unowned-because-UNADOPTED (the entire discovery corpus, Generated/CANDIDATE) is CORRECT — the promotion ladder working, since a candidate with an owner would be adoption smuggled past the gate. Unowned-while-OPERATING (exactly one instance found: the Runtime Adapter, RO-4) is the genuine defect class and is already docketed. This reframes the programme's recurring 'ownership-gap pattern': most of it was never a gap; the anomaly list shrinks to one item.

rationale_evidence.statement: An explicit argument against a governance anti-pattern (unbounded re-review loops), used to recommend accepting a repaired chain rather than commissioning a further independent review when the finding->repair->evidence->re-verification traceability chain is already intact.

rationale_evidence.anchor: AI: discover evidence, formulate questions, construct causal hypotheses, identify assumptions, run analyses, expose uncertainty, generate options, simulate consequences -> HUMAN/GOVERNED JUDGMENT -> DECISION. ... The platform supplies the epistemic scaffolding. Governance supplies legitimate authority. The agent supplies reasoning assistance.
rationale_evidence.statement: AI architecture principle: an AI agent should not be the source of wisdom; it discovers evidence, formulates questions, constructs causal hypotheses, identifies assumptions, runs analyses, exposes uncertainty, generates options and simulates consequences, but human/governed judgment produces the decision -- the platform supplies epistemic scaffolding, governance supplies legitimate authority, the agent supplies reasoning assistance.
